_comment: TEMPLATE — do not copy this file into place by hand. Install it with `bash tools/install-hooks.sh`, which substitutes __REPO_ROOT__ for the real container root and MERGES these entries into the target settings file instead of overwriting it. Every entry is tagged 'claude-checkpoint-hooks'; the installer only ever replaces entries carrying that tag (or an entry invoking one of these scripts, tagged or not — see install-hooks.sh's LEGACY list), so a user's own permissions, env and other projects' hooks survive. SHARED ACROSS EVERY CHECKPOINT-MANAGED REPO IN THIS CONTAINER: the commands below glob every repo under the session root that has this same tools/hooks/ layout, so installing this ONCE (from any one of them) protects every project in the container, and each entry point aggregates all of them into ONE JSON object (see tools/hooks/emit.py — two objects do not parse, and that silently costs an entire session briefing). WHY NOT EACH REPO'S OWN .claude/settings.json: confirmed that Claude Code on the web does not load hooks from a repo that sits in a subdirectory of the session root — CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset and one project root is resolved for the whole session.

hooks.command: for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/brief.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # claude-checkpoint-hooks
hooks.statusMessage: Reading where the last session stopped...

hooks.command: for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/save.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # claude-checkpoint-hooks
for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/save.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # claude-checkpoint-hooks
for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/big.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # claude-checkpoint-hooks
hooks.statusMessage: Session is large - saving before compaction...
